hints: The gradient of a velocity-time graph represents acceleration: $a = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{t_2 - t_1}$.
walkthrough:
Use the definition of acceleration as the gradient of the velocity-time graph on the interval $[30, 35]$:
$$a = \frac{12 - V}{35 - 30} = 0.8$$
$$\frac{12 - V}{5} = 0.8$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the formula for uniform acceleration over a time interval:
$$a = \frac{v - u}{\Delta t}$$
On the interval from $t = 30\text{ s}$ to $t = 35\text{ s}$, the initial velocity is $V$, the final velocity is $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the duration is $\Delta t = 35 - 30 = 5\text{ s}$, and $a = 0.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Substitute the known values into the equation:
$$0.8 = \frac{12 - V}{5}$$
Multiply both sides by $5$:
$$0.8 \times 5 = 12 - V$$
$$4 = 12 - V$$
Rearrange to solve for $V$:
$$V = 12 - 4 = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: Calculate the area under each of the four sections of the velocity-time graph.
The areas of the last three sections are $25 \times 8 = 200\text{ m}$, $\frac{1}{2}(8 + 12) \times 5 = 50\text{ m}$, and $\frac{1}{2}(15)(12) = 90\text{ m}$.
The first section is a trapezium with area $\frac{1}{2}(U + 8) \times 5$.
Equate the sum of all four areas to $375\text{ m}$ and solve for $U$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area under the velocity-time graph for stages 2, 3, and 4:
$$\text{Stage 2 } (t = 5 \text{ to } 30): \quad 25 \times 8 = 200\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Stage 3 } (t = 30 \text{ to } 35): \quad \frac{1}{2}(8 + 12) \times 5 = 10 \times 5 = 50\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Stage 4 } (t = 35 \text{ to } 50): \quad \frac{1}{2}(15) \times 12 = 90\text{ m}$$

Express the area of stage 1 ($t = 0$ to $5$) as a trapezium:
$$\text{Stage 1}: \quad \frac{1}{2}(U + 8) \times 5 = 2.5(U + 8)$$

Sum the four areas and equate to the total distance $375\text{ m}$:
$$2.5(U + 8) + 200 + 50 + 90 = 375$$
$$2.5(U + 8) + 340 = 375$$
$$2.5(U + 8) = 35$$
$$U + 8 = \frac{35}{2.5} = 14 \implies U = 14 - 8 = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the relationship between displacement and the area under a velocity-time graph:
$$\text{Total distance} = \text{Area}_1 + \text{Area}_2 + \text{Area}_3 + \text{Area}_4 = 375\text{ m}$$

Evaluate the area for each segment of motion:
- Segment 1 ($0 \le t \le 5\text{ s}$, trapezium from $U$ to $V = 8$):
$$\text{Area}_1 = \frac{U + 8}{2} \times 5 = 2.5(U + 8)$$
- Segment 2 ($5 \le t \le 30\text{ s}$, rectangle at constant speed $8$):
$$\text{Area}_2 = (30 - 5) \times 8 = 25 \times 8 = 200\text{ m}$$
- Segment 3 ($30 \le t \le 35\text{ s}$, trapezium from $8$ to $12$):
$$\text{Area}_3 = \frac{8 + 12}{2} \times (35 - 30) = \frac{20}{2} \times 5 = 10 \times 5 = 50\text{ m}$$
- Segment 4 ($35 \le t \le 50\text{ s}$, triangle from $12$ to $0$):
$$\text{Area}_4 = \frac{1}{2} \times (50 - 35) \times 12 = \frac{1}{2} \times 15 \times 12 = 15 \times 6 = 90\text{ m}$$

Add the known constant areas:
$$\text{Area}_2 + \text{Area}_3 + \text{Area}_4 = 200 + 50 + 90 = 340\text{ m}$$

Solve for the unknown initial speed $U$:
$$2.5(U + 8) + 340 = 375$$
Subtract $340$ from both sides:
$$2.5(U + 8) = 35$$
Divide by $2.5$:
$$U + 8 = \frac{35}{2.5} = 14$$
Subtract $8$:
$$U = 14 - 8 = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
